minutes.headline: Water district reviewed a PFAS treatment study proposal and agreed to charge the new project fee per unit, not per account.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District spent the first part of the meeting with consultants on a PFAS treatment study: bid prices, state revolving fund timing, the water protection bylaw, buying water from neighbors, and class action money. The board then took up the auditor's engagement letter, how the new Massapoag project charge on water bills should apply by unit, project progress, and replacing an old dump truck. Only the auditor motion is clearly a motion; its result is not in the captions.

budget_items.what_was_said: The charge would be applied per unit rather than per account, which would lower the average amount; commercial to stay at the flat rate for now.

what_happened.line: The board agreed to apply the new Massapoag project charge on water bills per unit rather than per account, at the current rate for the next bills.
Commercial accounts stay at the flat rate for now, and the final charge will be set once the bonding is known.
After reviewing a PFAS treatment study proposal with consultants, the board asked for a revised proposal before the full board meets in two weeks.
The consultant was also asked to bring funding options to the next meeting.
A motion let the acting chair sign the annual audit engagement letter, but the result is not audible in the captions; the superintendent will price larger dump trucks.

why_it_matters: Charging the Massapoag project fee per unit instead of per account changes what each water customer pays, and it is expected to lower the average amount.
The PFAS treatment study is the first step toward a treatment plant, and the funding options due at the next meeting will show how a plant could be paid for through water rates.
watch_next: The revised PFAS study proposal and funding options, due before the full board meets in about two weeks.
The final project charge, which is to be set once the bonding is known.
